result:
All four cartas are implemented, but I couldn't build or render anything here, so none of it has been checked yet.

## Changed paths
- **New `src/components/composition/MenuCollection.astro`:** an authored carta with a `layout` prop (`ledger`, `front-page`, `frames`, `plate`).
  - **Preserved:** the section and module attributes, the `module-*` class, every `data-fact-id` and `data-fact-scope`, `data-offering-id`, `data-offering-scope` and `data-search`, the `[data-menu-tools]` block with `[data-menu-search]`, `[data-menu-category]` and `[data-menu-count]`, `.contextual-collection`, the `ContextualImage` slot bindings with linked credits, the native `<details class="dish-detail">`, the `?plato=` links, the noscript note and the h2 with its intro text.
  - **Removed:** the `01 / La carta de ejemplo` kicker and the `0N /` item numbers. The `Para elegir con ganas` eyebrow is dropped on the carta pages only.
  - **Added:** an empty `aria-hidden` leader span, used by 01 only.
- **New `src/design/menu-carta.css`:** the four layouts. Every rule is scoped under `.page-collection .menu-carta`, and filtered dishes are hidden with `display:none!important`.
- **`ExperienceComposition.astro`:** it picks the layout (Immersive→ledger, Masthead→front-page, EmberReel→frames, PlateStudy→plate) and appends the CSS only when a layout applies. Any other profile on a carta route keeps `ContextualModule` and its eyebrow.
- **`ArtisticPages.astro`:** the collection branch calls `MenuCollection` and omits the eyebrow when `e` is absent. Other pages are unchanged.
- **Not touched:** the selection page, `ContextualModule`, the existing CSS and both client files.

## The four layouts
- **01 ledger:** a printed sheet.
  - Name, dotted leader and right-aligned price share one row, with the category above in small caps.
  - Each dish's photo is the left cell of its row, with no gap between rows, so on desktop they read as one continuous strip.
  - On phones the strip narrows to 4.5rem beside the text. The page never shows a large repeated photo.
- **02 front-page:** while no filter is active, the first dish is the lead.
  - On desktop the lead is a 7/5 split with a 6px top rule, a 3–6rem vermilion name and a price in a vermilion block.
  - Below it are three columns separated by vertical rules, each with a photo on top, then name and price.
  - On phones the lead is a 4:3 photo with a large name. The rest are compact rows with a small square photo on the right.
- **03 frames:** one frame per dish, with the photo and an ember underline.
  - The photo ratio is 3:2 on phones, 16:9 up to 1024px and 2:1 above that. I used 2:1 instead of 21:9 so the round pizza and pasta stay legible.
  - Name and price share the caption line. The description sits on the left and the details and select button on the right at 641px and up, stacked on phones.
- **04 plate:** a 36rem centred column.
  - Small matted photos sit above a centred Bodoni name, an italic category line, and the price under a short wine rule.
  - Odd dishes get a narrow 4:5 plate and wide spacing, even dishes a square plate and tighter spacing. Everything is centred, including the details.

## Filtered and empty states
The lead, column rules and plate offsets apply only when `data-collection-state` is not `filtered`, so every visible item gets the plain layout. A single filtered dish has no leftover lead or column offsets. When everything is hidden the container is flex or grid with no borders, margins or min-height of its own.

## Risks to check in the browser
- **Cascade:** legacy `.contextual-collection`, `.collection-tools` and `.semantic-v2` rules live in long CSS lines I couldn't read. I set `display:block` and neutralised padding on the carta section, but the rest of `.menu-carta` section/tool styling is unconfirmed.
- **01:** the photo column is `min-height:11rem` (9rem on phones). If the text is shorter than that, the strip shows only a thin crop of the photo.
- **02:** the three-column rule offsets assume exactly four dishes in the unfiltered state.
- **03:** the `.art-EmberReel` rail and the `--display` font stack could change heading wrapping in the caption line.
- **04:** the photo mat is hardcoded `#fbf6ec`, taken from the existing selection panel.
- **Tests:** any test asserting the old kicker, `0N /` numbers or the old `collection-item` classes on these four pages will now see a difference.
